candidates.title: National Television Multiple Ownership Rule
candidates.raw_excerpt: In this document, the Federal Communications Commission (Commission) repeals the national television multiple ownership rule (national cap), which prohibits a commercial television licensee from having a cognizable interest in television stations that have an aggregate national audience reach above 39%. The Commission finds, given seismic changes in the modern media marketplace, that the rule's repeal will help empower local broadcast television stations to operate in the public interest and to better serve the needs and interests of their local communities. The Commission will review on a case-by-case basis proposed transactions that would have been prohibited under the national cap to determine whether a proposed transaction would serve the Commission's media ownership goals of localism, competition, and viewpoint diversity.

candidates.raw_excerpt: As more information comes out about Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s numerous affairs with high-profile figures in the tech world, calls are mounting for the embattled chief to resign from his post. So far, numerous members of congress from both sides of the aisle have been joined by media figures like Fox Business host Larry Kudlow in calling for Huang to step down from what is arguably one of the most powerful posts in the world right now. Publications like the Economist have also issued blistering editorials calling for his resignation, characterizing Huang as a “brilliant man — and a fool.” The snafu all stems from reporting by the Financial Times , which recently unveiled that one of Huang’s affairs was with the executive of a Singaporean AI company named Alice Huang. Per the FT ’s reporting, anonymous sources in the US intelligence community believe the woman is a spy for the Chinese government — claims that sparked a massive debate around Nvidia’s central position in the world economy. Setting aside the putrid ethics of cheating on your spouse , whether Huang’s mistress was really a Chinese operative remains to be seen. For starters, the evidence traces back to anonymous US intelligence agents, the kind who have been known to sensationalize when it comes to tales of Chinese spies in high places (China firmly denied the accusation, dismissing it as a smear tactic by the West.) Beyond Huang, this wouldn’t be the first time the AI industry has had a freakout about seductive honeys from foreign lands, a tacitly xenophobic narrative drawn from Cold War pulp novels. And from another point of view, Huang’s ousting may come at the perfect time. Financial markets are experiencing turmoil as fears around a hyperinflated AI bubble become mainstream . If someone in Huang’s position was ever going to get out while the getting is good, it seems now would be the time — though given how topsy-turvy this saga has been already, what the AI chip billionaire does next is anyone’s guess

candidates.raw_excerpt: A long-term goal at NASA has been the ability to robotically haul back to Earth specimens from the Red Planet. candidates.raw_excerpt: On Nov. 11, 1966, the Gemini 12 mission launched an astronaut crew into orbit and set the stage for NASA's Apollo program to land humans on the moon. Gemini 12 was the last mission of the Gemini program. It had two astronauts on board: Jim Lovell and Buzz Aldrin . NASA wanted to send humans to the moon. But first, it needed to make sure crews had the right skills, like docking vehicles in space and taking spacewalks. Before Gemini 12, astronauts struggled with spacewalks because there weren't enough handholds on their spacecraft. NASA made some spacewalk changes for Gemini 12. Aldrin performed three spacewalks and spent more than five hours working in space with no major problems. Gemini 12 also successfully docked to an unpiloted Agena booster that launched the same day. The astronauts returned to Earth after four days in space. Both Aldrin and Lovell went on to join the Apollo program . Aldrin became the second person to walk on the moon during Apollo 11 , and Lovell became the commander of Apollo 13 . The Gemini 12 astronauts James Lovell and Edwin Aldrin lifted off aboard a Titan launch vehicle from the Kennedy Space Center on November 11, 1966, an hour and a half after their Agena target vehicle was orbited by an Atlas rocket. (Image credit: NASA/MSFC) Why it mattered Gemini 12 may have closed out NASA's Gemini program of two-person space missions, but it established the mission also established the fundamentals of spacewalking that Apollo astronauts would use when they walked on the moon. It's fitting that Aldrin was the primary spacewalker of the mission. A rookie astronaut (and the first to earn a Ph.D.), Aldrin set a precedent by training for his spacewalk in a neutral buoyancy pool in Maryland to better simulate working in weightlessness. candidates.title: Hubble Space Telescope reveals glittering stars with mysterious origins | Space photo of the day for Nov. 11, 2026
candidates.raw_excerpt: The Hubble Space Telescope has captured a breathtaking view of thousands of stars glittering like cosmic jewels in a dazzling display of blue, gold and orange. But this spectacular scene is far more than just a pretty picture. Some of these stars are almost as old as the universe itself and could hold clues to how our Milky Way formed. M30 is a globular star cluster located approximately 27,500 light-years from Earth. (Image credit: ESA/Hubble & NASA, M. Libralato, G. Piotto, A. Sarajedini) What is it? The exquisite image released by ESA on Nov. 5 shows Messier 30 (M30), a densely packed collection of stars located approximately 27,500 light-years from Earth in the constellation Capricornus. M30 is a globular cluster, a roughly spherical collection of tens of thousands to millions of stars held together by gravity . Our Milky Way is home to at least 150 of these ancient stellar gatherings, some of which are estimated to be between 11.5 billion and 13.5 billion years old. For comparison, the universe itself is approximately 13.8 billion years old! Why is it amazing Besides looking like a vast cosmic treasure trove glittering across the universe, M30 also has a fascinating story to tell. Globular clusters are essentially cosmic time capsules. Their ancient stars preserve chemical clues about the conditions that existed when they formed, helping astronomers piece together the Milky Way's early history. Astronomers have also discovered that M30, along with several other globular clusters, traverses the Milky Way in the opposite direction to the galaxy's rotation. This unusual motion raises the intriguing possibility that M30 may not have formed in our galaxy at all. It could have simply been captured by the Milky Way billions of years ago.

candidates.title: NASA's new UVEX space telescope will peer deep into the universe's most violent events
candidates.raw_excerpt: A new NASA space telescope will study the universe in ultraviolet light to reveal the violent and turbulent events that bubble under what appears to be a cosmic sea of tranquility. The Ultraviolet Explorer (UVEX) mission, developed by NASA in conjunction with the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), will be the first mission to create deep all-sky maps in ultraviolet light. Thus, when it launches in 2031, UVEX will join new sky-mapping surveys like NASA's SPHEREx (Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer), which scans the cosmos in infrared, and the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, which does the same over the southern hemisphere in visible light, in creating deep-sky maps across a broad swathe of the electromagnetic spectrum. UVEX's ultraviolet views will reveal explosive events such as the collisions between ultra-dense stellar corpses called neutron stars and the supernova explosions that mark the deaths of massive stars and the births of neutron stars and black holes. Additionally, the NASA ultraviolet telescope should be able to detect a multitude of low-mass galaxies much closer to the Milky Way than similar galaxies that are currently being observed millions and even billions of light-years away by NASA's James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) . The $590 million UVEX mission will "advance fundamental frontiers in astrophysics, from understanding the smallest galaxies to diagnosing the aftermath of neutron-star mergers and other cosmic explosions," the mission's principal investigator, Caltech physics professor Fiona Harrison, said in an Oct. 27 statement . "The first major ultraviolet space mission in two decades, UVEX is a bold leap forward in our exploration of the ultraviolet universe," Caltech President Ray Jayawardhana said in the same statement. candidates.raw_excerpt: Credit: DLR A fire at an external contractor’s facility has delayed the installation of a containerised greenhouse designed to simulate growing crops on the Moon. According to a response to a parliamentary inquiry published by the German Bundesta g on 20 October, a fire occurred while the EDEN-LUNA greenhouse container was being refurbished. The incident has pushed back the planned installation at the LUNA facility in Cologne, which was initially expected to be completed in 2026. The installation is now expected to take place in the second quarter of 2027. The German Aerospace Center (DLR) initially acknowledged that the installation would not take place until 2027 in a statement published on 4 September. It did not, however, provide a reason for the delay until prompted by a parliamentary inquiry submitted by members of the Alternative for Germany (AfD) party. While the response to the parliamentary inquiry acknowledged the fire, it did not provide details about the extent of the damage or specify what had been damaged. The EDEN-LUNA greenhouse is being developed by DLR to study potential technologies for growing fresh food during extended missions to the Moon and Mars. The project builds on the agency’s EDEN ISS greenhouse, which was operated near Germany’s Neumayer III research station in Antarctica between 2018 and 2022. Following the conclusion of the Antarctic campaign, the greenhouse was dismantled and transported back to Germany in April 2023. Since then, DLR has been refurbishing and upgrading the facility at its Institute of Space Systems in Bremen in preparation for a second experimental campaign under the EDEN-LUNA programme. His explanation built on NASA’s previously announced decision to abandon SLS Block 1B and its Exploration Upper Stage (EUS) . The emphasis was on improving the hardware and operations available now while preparing for a later transition. “There are a lot of ways to shake the $4 billion disposable rocket label that SLS has carried and one of which is launch more frequently,” Isaacman said. “There is nothing about pushing it off into next year that makes anything cost less,” he added. Centaur V and a standardized SLS Artemis IV was previously intended to introduce Block 1B and EUS. NASA instead moved toward a near-Block 1 configuration using Centaur V, avoiding continued development of an upper stage dedicated to SLS. Centaur V is already in production for United Launch Alliance’s Vulcan rocket . It first flew on Vulcan’s Cert-1 mission in January 2024 , while the broader Centaur family provides decades of flight heritage. However, the stretched version planned for NASA remains in development. Isaacman said NASA originally intended to use the existing Centaur configuration, but pursued the higher-performance version as part of efforts to move Orion closer to the Moon and simplify the landers’ task. candidates.raw_excerpt:
China has completed a 1,000-kilometer hollow-core fiber transmission verification, marking a new breakthrough in key technologies for next-generation communication networks.

The verification, jointly conducted by China Telecom, Yangtze Optical Fibre and Cable (YOFC), and ZTE over a 1,007.48-kilometer fiber link, achieved simultaneous bidirectional signal transmission at 64 Tb per second in each direction, equivalent to supporting the upload and download of 160 films in 4K resolution per second, according to China Telecom on November 4.

The vast majority of optical fibers in widespread use are solid-core fibers, in which signals travel through a quartz glass core at 200,000 kilometers per second, whereas hollow-core fibers carry signals mainly through air channels at close to 300,000 kilometers per second.

This shortens transmission time and lowers latency. A signal takes just 3.43 milliseconds to travel one way across the 1,000-kilometer link, according to test technicians.

The technology doubles transmission capacity and extends transmission distance by 60 percent compared with the best-performing solid-core fibers currently available, according to the technicians.

Some people worried that it might crash into a populated area. However, the small spacecraft broke up in the atmosphere and didn't cause any property damage. It disintegrated about 50 miles above the Falkland Islands in the South Atlantic Ocean. The European Space Agency called the mission a success. GOCE lasted far longer than expected. TOI-2535 b was routinely observed with NASA's Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite ( TESS ) space telescope for seven years between April 2019 and March 2026 as it completed its 8.25-Earth day orbit of its parent star. That's 10 times quicker than the orbit of Mercury around the sun and means this blisteringly hot planet is classed as a " hot Jupiter ." However, something strange happened started to happen as astronomers observed the distant world. The orbits of the planet weren't regular like those of other planets, with TOI-2535 b often arriving six hours early or six hours later than when astronomers expected. Then, in March this year, TESS was no longer spotting the characteristic drops in starlight that TOI-2535 b caused as it crossed, or "transited," the face of its parent star. It seemed to have vanished. This team used TESS data to determine that TOI-2535 b is being pulled on by an unseen neighbor and is, in turn, pulling on that planet as well. candidates.title: Uranus has a weird magnetic field that's stumped scientists for 40 years — we may finally know why
candidates.raw_excerpt: The posided magnetic fields of Uranus and Neptune may stem from extreme conditions lying within their deep interior. Unravelling the mystery behind the magnetic fields of these worlds is giving us new insight into the little-known interiors of the ice giants. Only one spacecraft has ever visited Uranus and Neptune, the Voyager 2 spacecraft which spend past Uranus in January 1986 and Neptune in August 1989. Voyager 2 found that their planetary magnetic fields were, to put it bluntly, wonky. Uranus’ magnetic field was offset from its rotational axis by 59 degrees and isn’t even centered on the planet’s core, but instead is only two-thirds of the way down. Neptune is similar, with a disordered magnetic field offset by 47 degrees and centered halfway between the core and its visible cloud tops. candidates.raw_excerpt: NASA’s Mars rover Curiosity acquired this close-up image using its Mars Hand Lens Imager, showing the abundance of disc-shaped potential crystal forms on our next drill target, dubbed "Nazca." (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS) NASA's Curiosity Mars rover is sizing up its next dig site on the Red Planet. The Curiosity team will characterize the surface composition of the Mars site, informally named "Nazca," as thoroughly as possible before drilling into it. What is it? Curiosity snapped the close-up image on Oct. 18, 2026, using its Mars Hand Lens Imager (MAHLI). The image shows multiple roughly disk-shaped potential crystal formations at the rover's next drill target. MAHLI is located on the turret at the end of the rover's robotic arm. It uses an onboard focusing process to make a composite of images of the same target acquired at different positions to focus on multiple features in a single image. Why is it incredible? Scientists theorize that the "discs and needles" texture takes its characteristic shape as crystals, or "crystal forms," grow. The relatively large sizes of the crystal forms at "Nazca" may provide clues about the temperatures at which they grew, as well as information about the abundance of salts and fluids in the area at the time. Complicating this picture, however, is the fact that mineral crystals can be replaced by other minerals after their original crystallization. The new minerals are known as "pseudomorphs," because they have the same shape as the original minerals but not the same composition or molecular structure. The Curiosity team will characterize the surface composition of Nazca — which shares its name with an ancient South American civilization that's famous for the large designs it etched into the rock and dirt — before drilling begins. The NASA researchers will then be able to compare the deeper composition to the surface-level composition.

But rather than head straight to Mars, the two spacecraft dawdled through a looping trajectory . Now, they are back in Earth's neighborhood where they tackled a crucial engine burn unusually close to Earth that — if all goes well — will set them on track for Mars . "No NASA mission has ever done this before," said Rob Lillis, a planetary and space physicist at the University of California, Berkeley and principal investigator of the ESCAPADE mission. "For most missions, it just isn't necessary." That's because traditionally NASA's Mars missions have been carefully choreographed within cosmic launch constraints, leaving Earth during a brief window of planetary alignment that only occurs every 26 months.
